Hi Anita / Michael —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Scope we covered: PII types (customer names, emails, payment metadata), data retention expectations (7 years historical logs vs 90-day default), and logging/obfuscation needs for support traces.
- Encryption asks you raised: in-transit TLS, at-rest disk encryption, and a requirement to support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production tokens and logs.

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- CMK scope: we want CMKs for customer PII persistence (name/email) and for API tokens stored in your vault. Audit logs should be encrypted with a platform key but we need the ability to export logs encrypted under our key for long-term retention.
- Retention: logs for support/debugging can be 90 days, but regulatory logs (payment reconciliation) need 7 years.
- Residency: yes, primary storage in us-west. We also require a documented process for creating any DR backups outside us-west — must be manual and require security approval.

Can you and your SEs confirm whether Redwood supports: 
1) Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via AWS KMS import or external HSM integration?
2) Envelope encryption for large artifact storage (s3 / object-store)?
3) Key rotation procedures and whether rotation can be customer-triggered?

Appreciate it — I’ll share our security questionnaire if you need more detail.

—Michael
Head of Platform Security | Paywise
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@paywise.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@paywise.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Encryption & KMS options for Paywise (Next steps)

Great questions — looping in our SE and infra leads to answer precisely. High-level answers below; Dev / Rishi will follow with technical notes and a proposed architecture diagram.

1) BYOK / HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys. For cloud deployments we integrate with customer AWS KMS keys (BYOK) and provide a roadmap for HSM-backed keys via CloudHSM or third-party HSMs for Dedicated / Private deployments. The attached design doc includes the integration flow and permissions required (redwood_kms_design.pdf).

2) Envelope encryption: yes — we use envelope encryption for large objects and model artifacts. The platform master key encrypts data keys which then encrypt objects. Customers can optionally bring the top-level CMK to control the envelope key wrapping.

3) Rotation: keys can be rotated on a schedule. For CMKs we support rotation via your KMS (customer-triggered rotation supported where KMS provider permits). For platform-managed keys we can execute rotations with a maintenance window; we also maintain key versioning to re-encrypt at rest without downtime when possible.

Residency / backups: we can enforce region-restricted backups. Any cross-region DR snapshots are gated behind an approval workflow and will be captured in the compliance playbook that we’ll share.

Next steps:
- Dev & Rishi to propose a short 45-min technical deep dive next Tue/Wed — can you share slots?
- I’ll upload a concise architecture diagram to the Drive link and drop a trimmed SOC2 evidence pack for the specific checklist items you requested.

Attachments: network-diagram.png (arch draft)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdE

Thanks — Marissa
